messages:
sara: Quick sanity check: ran inference sweeps for Llama family across PCIe and SXM nodes in us-west and eu-west. Seeing weird tail latencies on PCIe when NVLink absent even for 2-GPU runs. Anyone else?

owen: Can you paste the run config? which kernels, pinned or not?

sara: Here's the basic config I used:
```
model: llama-70b-v3
batch: 4
seq: 1024
kernel_priority: fused-attn-v2,matmul-fused
num_gpus: 2
pinning: NUMA socket0
env: KV_CACHE=on CONT_BATCH=enabled
```

jin: If NVLink is present cross-GPU copy ~20us, on plain PCIe same payload -> ~90us. That explains the tail. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

perf-bot: throughput_summary: us-west-sxm=430 tok/s, us-west-pcie=320 tok/s, eu-west-sxm=410 tok/s, eu-west-pcie=315 tok/s | p99_latency_ms: sxm=230ms pcie=480ms

owen: Did you try turning continuous batching off? that sometimes hides KV cache sync issues on PCIe

sara: Yep — toggled it. continuous batching reduces per-token cost but increases tail on PCIe under heavy cross-GPU sync. Quick log snippet:
```
[run] kv_cache_hit_rate=0.92
[latency] p50=18ms p90=90ms p99=480ms
[kernel] selected=fused-attn-v2 fallback=matmul-fused (seq>2048)
```

jin: NUMA pinning helped ~15% p99 on our SXM boxes. bind process + CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, and pin GPU memory affinity.
example: `taskset -c 0-15 ./serve --model ...` and `export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1`

alexa: Also saw kernel fallback on PCIe when seq > 2048 — runtime picks non-fused matmul and perf drops massively. Check `/var/log/redwood/runtime/kernel_selection.log` for hints.

sara: I'll run a focused sweep: (1) force NUMA pinning, (2) force kernel selector to prefer fused-attn where possible, (3) compare NVLink vs PCIe across regions, then run quantized 4-bit to see quality/perf tradeoff. Will post charts.

owen: pls include per-step traces, KV hit rates, and region tags — infra variance matters. thx

sara: 👍 thanks all, will share results later today.
